title: Fake Proof of Address: How to Spot It and What It Can't Prove
summary: How to spot a fake proof of address across utility bills, leases, and statements, and what US CIP actually requires for an address.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** A fake proof of address is a utility bill, bank statement, lease, or similar document, edited after issue or generated from scratch, that places a person or business at an address they do not occupy.[FinCEN's analysis of 2021 filings](https://fincen.gov/sites/default/files/shared/FTA_Identity_Final508.pdf) linked about 1.6 million BSA reports, 42% of the total, to identity-related suspicious activity, a broad figure covering far more than address documents. The US CIP rule requires a bank to collect an address and names no proof-of-address document, so the decision should turn on whether independent records place the customer there.


## What a Fake Proof of Address Actually Is


Proof of address is a role a document plays, and many document types can fill it. A fake proof of address is any of them misrepresented to support a location claim: a fake electricity bill, a statement with a changed mailing address, a lease for a tenancy that never existed. Document-specific checks live in their own guides:[how to spot a fake utility bill](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-utility-bill) ,[how to spot a fake lease agreement](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-lease-agreement) , and[how to spot a fake bank statement](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-bank-statement) . This page covers the decision above them: which document to accept, how much weight it can carry, and what to do when it disagrees with other records.


Each type comes from a different issuer, and the issuer determines how the document can be tested.


Document Usual issuer Where to confirm it Main limitation


Electricity, gas, or water bill Utility provider The provider, or a data source showing service at the address Shows a billing relationship, which may be old or shared


Bank statement Bank or credit union The issuer, or a consumer reporting source Repeats the address the account holder gave the bank


Lease Landlord or property manager The owner of record, contacted independently A private contract with no institution behind it


Mortgage statement Loan servicer County property records and the servicer Ownership does not show who lives there


Driver's license or state ID State agency Consumer report or other database The printed address can lag a move


Insurance policy, voter or vehicle registration Insurer or government office The issuer or public record Coverage varies and records can be out of date


Acceptance lists differ by institution, and each reflects whoever wrote it. The US Postal Service's application to operate a commercial mail receiving agency, for example, accepts a current lease, a mortgage or deed of trust, a voter or vehicle registration card, or a home or vehicle insurance policy as address verification.


## Edited Files and Generated Files


Address fraud arrives in two production classes, and they fail different tests.


An edited-after-creation file began as a real document. Someone changed the name, the address, or the date and saved it again. Most of the page is genuine and the issuer's formatting survives. The altered field often stops agreeing with something elsewhere in the file or in the file's own history.


A generated-from-scratch file never came from the claimed issuer. It can be internally tidy because all of it was composed at once. It tends to lack the production history of the issuer's own output, or it shares structure with other files built the same way.


A third category needs separate treatment: a genuine, unaltered document that belongs to someone else or describes an address the applicant left. File analysis has nothing to find, because the file is authentic. Only the claim is false.


## Tells That Work Across Document Types


The checks that transfer between document types are the ones that test the address claim. Recency compares the issue date with any policy window and with the period the document describes. Name matching against the application catches more than a glance at the page. Issuer plausibility asks whether this organization could have sent this document to this location, which for a utility means whether it serves the area at all.


Logos, fonts, and overall polish say little, since an edited file inherits the issuer's design and generated files copy public branding. A document that looks right has passed nothing.


When an applicant submits several documents, compare them with each other. Unrelated issuers have no reason to share a template or production pattern, so similarities are worth recording. Documents that agree perfectly are weak corroboration if all of them came from the applicant.


## When the Address Meets Other Records


The most useful test of an address happens outside the document. The federal[Identity Theft Red Flags guidelines at 16 CFR Part 681](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/appendix-A_to_part_681) list illustrative warning signs that translate directly into review steps:


- A consumer reporting agency returns a notice of address discrepancy.
- The address does not match any address in the consumer report.
- The address was used on a previous fraudulent application.
- The address is fictitious, a mail drop, or a prison.
- The address is shared with an unusually large number of other applicants or customers.
- Documents provided for identification appear altered or forged.


A mismatch needs interpretation. Consumer report data can lag a real move, so an unmatched address is a reason to ask for more and a poor reason on its own to decline.


Address type deserves its own check. The Postal Service defines a commercial mail receiving agency as a business that accepts mail for others as a service, and it classes office business centers and reshipping services the same way. A genuine document can be correctly addressed to one of these locations while the customer neither lives nor operates there. For a business, the question becomes whether the address functions as a place of business or only receives mail.


Repetition across a portfolio is the signal a single reviewer cannot see. One application at an address is unremarkable. Dozens at the same address under different names is a case. In its 2021 data, FinCEN counted about 423,000 reports involving false records and found that 13% of identity-related reports described attackers exploiting insufficient verification processes.


## What an Address Document Can and Can't Establish


An authentic address document establishes a narrow fact: an issuer, at some date, associated a name with a location. It does not show that the person presenting it is the person named, that the person lives there today, or that the address is a home rather than a mailbox. Forensic review can show that a file is unaltered. Occupancy has to be confirmed some other way.


US law asks for less than many onboarding checklists assume. Under[31 CFR 1020.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-B/section-1020.220) , a bank must obtain an address before opening an account. For an individual, that means a residential or business street address, with an APO or FPO box number or the street address of next of kin or another contact as the fallback. For an entity, it means a principal place of business, local office, or other physical location. The rule is written for banks, and other sectors have their own CIP rules.


Verification runs on a different standard. The bank must verify enough to form a reasonable belief that it knows the customer's true identity, and the[FFIEC BSA/AML Manual](https://bsaaml.ffiec.gov/manual/AssessingComplianceWithBSARegulatoryRequirements/01) states that a bank need not establish the accuracy of every element of identifying information. The rule's documentary examples are an unexpired government-issued ID evidencing nationality or residence, and entity documents such as certified articles of incorporation. Utility bills and leases do not appear in that text. Non-documentary methods include contacting the customer and comparing the information against a consumer reporting agency, public database, or other source.


A proof-of-address requirement is therefore usually the institution's own policy. The FFIEC Manual encourages reviewing more than one document given the availability of counterfeit ones, and the CIP record must describe the resolution of any substantive discrepancy, so an address conflict needs a written outcome. The June 27, 2025 exemption order concerned TIN collection and left the address requirement alone.


## What to Do With a Suspect File


Separate two questions: whether this file is genuine, and whether this customer is at this address. The first belongs to file review. The second needs records the applicant does not control.


Keep the original upload, because screenshots and re-exports remove file history. Request the native file when the submission is a photo or flattened image. To read the production history,[x-ray the file](https://sphinxhq.com/products/doc-fraud) and record the outcome by class of signal.


Then confirm independently. Compare the address against a consumer reporting source, a public database, or the owner of record, and reach any issuer or landlord through contact details found separately from the document. For higher-risk relationships, a code mailed to the address tests whether someone can receive mail there, which still falls short of proving residence.


When the file shows editing or generation and nothing independent supports the address, stop relying on it. The CIP rule requires procedures for when a bank cannot form a reasonable belief, including when not to open an account and when to file a SAR. Avoid telling an applicant which signal failed.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How can you tell if a proof of address is fake?


Check whether the date, name, and issuer fit the claim, then examine the file's production history for signs of editing or generation. Finally compare the address against sources the applicant does not control, such as a consumer report or public record.


### Does a bank have to collect proof of address in the US?


Under 31 CFR 1020.220, a bank must obtain a street address, or the permitted fallback, before opening an account. The rule names no utility bill or similar document, and it allows verification through government ID and non-documentary methods. Institutions can still require proof of address under their own risk-based policy.


### How do you spot a fake electricity bill?


Test the service dates, usage, charges, and whether the provider serves that address, then check the file's history and an independent source. A real provider and a tidy layout do not settle it, since a generated bill can copy both.


### Is a P.O. box acceptable as an address for CIP?


For an individual, the CIP rule calls for a residential or business street address, with an APO or FPO box number or the street address of next of kin or another contact as the fallback. Agency FAQs accept a rural route number or a description of physical location, and distinguish a rural route from a post office box.
